source.title: Deep linear networks for regression are implicitly regularized towards flat minima

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: Tests learning-rate effects on training and sharpness in deep linear regression, a different model and setting from V5.
record.gate_note: Results are for regression with quadratic loss, not CIFAR classification. Figure 1 reports training distance and sharpness; Figure 2 reports learning-rate thresholds across depths. Figure 3 reports divergence probability by initialization scale and learning rate, but provides no textual values.
record.test_reason: The study measures successful training beyond the initial sharpness stability threshold and edge-of-stability dynamics in deep linear regression, a new setting for V5. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record describes the learning-rate experiments reasonably, but omits the main conclusion: gradient flow in deep linear regression converges under stated small-scale or residual initialization assumptions and selects minimizers with sharpness within a condition-number-dependent factor of the minimum. Small-scale solutions have approximately rank-one, aligned weights. Finite-step gradient-descent experiments illustrate successful training beyond initial stability, edge-of-stability behavior in some conditions, and a critical rate related to minimum minimizer sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: Deep linear univariate regression with quadratic loss; the cited V5 recipes concern wide networks and full-batch sharpness behavior. Experiments use gradient descent; theoretical results concern gradient flow.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate, initialization scale, and depth affect training success or divergence; the study reports the critical rate as independent of initialization scale in Figure 1a.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient flow converges under the stated initialization assumptions and selects minimizers whose sharpness is within a condition-number-dependent factor of minimum achievable sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep linear regression trained by gradient flow has an initialization-dependent implicit bias toward relatively flat global minima.

record.problems: The experimental plots show confidence intervals for Figures 1a and 1b, but exact values are not stated in the text. Figures 1c and 1d show selected single runs. Main theoretical convergence results concern gradient flow, while the experiments use gradient descent. The study uses a small univariate regression setup, not classification benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No result-bearing rows omitted. Figure 4–5 repeat analogous residual-initialization experiments; they are not extracted because the text gives no distinct qualitative claim beyond the Figure 1 behavior and the plotted values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Convolutional classification networks, CIFAR-10/100, training classification error, random labels and model-size comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the benefit of additional student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, learning-speed comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional trainability.

The wide-network regime; a directly documented brief loss rise followed by curvature reduction and low loss; extended-time loss trajectories; and divergence explicitly shown to start below the initial stability threshold.
Batch normalization versus otherwise comparable networks, higher-rate tolerance attributable to normalization, and Fixup speed and stability comparisons.

missing.what: Initial and final sharpness in Figure 1b: successful training can begin above 2/η; final sharpness increases with initialization scale and plateaus at 2/η. Record this alongside R1 and identify survivor conditioning.
missing.locator: Introduction, discussion of Figures 1a–1b; Figure 1b; Appendix C

missing.what: Nonlinear GELU MLP results: with noiseless data, final sharpness plateaus at 2/η for large initialization and remains below it for small initialization; with noisy data, authors report reaching 2/η for every tested rate and scale. These are endpoint measurements, not full edge-of-stability trajectories.

Underdetermined linear regression shows a qualitatively similar relationship between learning rate, initialization scale and initial/final sharpness, extending the endpoint observations to n = 15, d = 20, L = 5.
missing.locator: Appendix C, Underdetermined regression and link to generalization; Figure 6a

record.verdict_notes: No challenges verdict is warranted: failure above a critical learning rate agrees with V5, and the text does not establish divergence from below the initial stability threshold. Figures 4–5 are declared in rows_left_out and therefore are not listed as missing. Exact plotted probabilities and trajectory values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Classification error, CIFAR-10/100, corrupted or random labels, and model size comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width.
Plain versus residual convolutional classification networks and training error.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons and trainable depth in plain nonlinear networks.
Wide networks and the initial linearized model's stability limit are not tested directly; no sharpness threshold tracking over longer full-batch runs.
Batch normalization comparisons and accuracy-speed measures.
